speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Some of the participants in the LPA value chain have given feedback on the concern that LPA Certificate Issuers are merely rubber-stamping.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: While I do not think so, there is a possibility that that may happen in the future, especially in relation to LPA applications with the Government's push towards more LPAs and enhancement of knowledge of LPAs.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, can the Ministry consider looking into publishing more detailed guidance on the duties and responsibilities of Certificate Issuers in the making of LPAs?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: In fact, LPA Certificate Issuers play a very key role in the entire process.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: First of all, who can be a CI?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: It is not any Tom, Dick or Harry who can be a CI.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, first of all, the qualification to be a CI is already one step in ensuring that this is a professional service that is provided.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: And this process is an important safeguard in the LPA application process.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: What does a CI need to do in the entire process of discharging his or her duty?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: In that meet-up process, the CI also verifies the donors' identity.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I shall not go into details of how this is done.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Thereafter, when all these steps have been made, the donor then digitally signs the LPA in the presence of the CI.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: For the Member's assurance, we do currently have regular sessions where we meet up with the CIs through their respective professional organisations to reiterate the important role that the CIs play in this process.
